query: What does `git rebase --onto` do? Give one short example.
result:
`git rebase --onto <newbase> <upstream> [<branch>]` replays only the commits in `<upstream>..<branch>` on top of `<newbase>`. Unlike a plain `git rebase <base>`, it lets the new base differ from the commits' old base, so you can move a branch off a parent it was built on.

Example: `feature` was branched from `old-feature`, which has since been merged into `main`. To move only `feature`'s own commits onto `main`:

```bash
git rebase --onto main old-feature feature
```
